title: pvStreakLine
body:
## pvStreakLine

Computes streaklines in an unsteady (time-dependent) vector field: particles are released from every SeedSource point at each input time step and advected through the changing field, and the particles released from the same place are joined into lines, the analogue of continuous dye injection. ParaView requests the input time steps itself, from the first step up to the requested time, so the input must have at least two time steps and a 3-component point vector field. Output is polydata (polylines, single points as vertices) with ParticleAge, ParticleId, InjectedPointId and the interpolated input arrays. Use pvStreamTracer for a steady snapshot and pvTemporalParticlesToPathlines to draw trails of existing particles.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- In the VTK used by ParaView 5.13.3 the streakline filter forces reinjection at every step, so ForceReinjectionEveryNSteps has no effect here; StaticSeeds and DisableResetCache are also no-ops.
- Every requested time integrates from the first time step, which is slow on long series; restrict the input time range first.
- Velocity must be point data; convert cell-centred solver output with cellToPoint.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `StreakLine`. Identity: `filters/StreakLine`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input list for the native Input port. List each upstream node to connect; each entry is a node name or a {node, port} object. ParaView: Specify which is the Input of the StreamTracer filter. Accepted data: any data object (vtkDataObject). The input needs at least one point-centred array with 3 components. | True | nonempty list | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":true,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataObject"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |
| `SeedSource` | Required data input list for the native SeedSource port. List each upstream node to connect; each entry is a node name or a {node, port} object. Accepted data: any dataset (meshes, grids, point sets) (vtkDataSet). | True | nonempty list | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataSet"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ComputeVorticity` | Compute vorticity and angular rotation of particles as they progress | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `DisableResetCache` | Has no effect in ParaView 5.13.3: the VTK setter is an empty deprecated stub (caching is now automated) and the getter always returns false, so the cache is handled the same way whatever value is set here. ParaView's own text says it stops the cache being reset so that new computations start from previous results; that no longer happens through this setting. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `ForceReinjectionEveryNSteps` | Has no effect on this filter in ParaView 5.13.3: the streakline filter sets ForceReinjectionEveryNSteps to 1 every time it initialises, so particles are reinjected at every step whatever value is set here. ParaView's own text, which describes reinjection every Nth step, holds for the particle tracer (pvParticleTracer) but not for streaklines. | `{"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `InterpolatorType` | This property determines which interpolator to use for evaluating the velocity vector field. The first is faster though the second is more robust in locating cells during streamline integration. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Interpolator with Point Locator","Interpolator with Cell Locator"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Interpolator with Point Locator"` |
| `MeshOverTime` | The input mesh can either be 1) different over time, or 2) static over time, or 3) a linear transformation of the first time step over time, or 4) have the same topology over time. If a value other than Different are used, then performance can be improved significantly because certain data structures, such as locators or cell links are not rebuilt for each timestep. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Different","Static","Linear Transformation","Same Topology"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Different"` |
| `SelectInputVectors` | Specify which vector array should be used for the integration through that filter. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"maxItems":2,"minItems":2,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE","REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `StaticSeeds` | Has no effect on this filter in ParaView 5.13.3: StaticSeeds is only initialised and printed by vtkParticleTracerBase, which the filter derives from, and nothing in it reads the value. Only the legacy tracers read it (pvLegacyParticlePath, pvLegacyStreakLine and pvInSituParticlePath). ParaView's own text says that setting it to 1 avoids repeated grid searches for unchanging seeds; that holds for those operations, not for this one. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvStreakLine",
  "inputs": {
    "Input": [
      "UPSTREAM_Input"
    ],
    "SeedSource": [
      "UPSTREAM_SeedSource"
    ]
  }
}
```
